course_description:
Introduction to physical and chemical processing of minerals and recycled materials to produce metals, alloys and metal compounds. Processing technologies used in minerals industry, their characteristics, how and why these processes are selected and factors affecting the choice of process route. Included are lessons on the economic, environmental, and social aspects of the metals industry.

The minerals industry provides the backbone to ﾠour modern industrialised society, providing the raw materials that we need to build our cities, and the devices we use to provide transport, communications and lifestyle. The processing of minerals and metals recycling is an activity of increasing importance. The industry offers a wide variety of career paths and opportunities for employment around the world.

This course provides an introduction to physical and chemical processing of minerals and recycled materials to produce metals and other valuable products, to recover energy and to minimise environmental impact.ﾠ Learn about:

The course is suitable for students undertaking programs inﾠ Chemical, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, Earth and Physical Sciences, and can be counted as ﾠcredit in these programs.

It is mandatory for each student enrolled in this course to take safety induction beforeﾠ undertaking the lab practicals.

course_aims:
The aims of this course are to:

• Introduce core processing technologies employed in the minerals and metal recycling industries, explaining their characteristics, applications and the fundamental physical and chemical principles that govern them.

• Identify and address the challenges in maintaining a sustainable supply of minerals and metals, addressing future industry needs and social and environmental impacts.

• Establish the groundwork for advanced mineral separation and metal extraction courses.

learning_outcomes.description: Master the fundamental principles governing physical and chemical processes involved in the selective separation of minerals from ores and the extraction of metals from mineral concentrates and recycled materials.
Apply these key principles effectively to separate minerals and extract metals in practical, real-world scenarios.
Develop practical proficiency in executing mineral separation and metal extraction techniques within a laboratory setting.

Analyse and recommend optimal “mine-to-metal” processing routes for specific ore deposits or secondary materials, considering factors such as economic viability, environmental impact, and social responsibility.
Collaborate effectively within a team to overcome metallurgical challenges and complete metallurgical tasks.
Produce high-quality written practical reports and deliver clear, well-structured oral presentations on metallurgical projects.

assessment_details.title: Tutorial Assignments
assessment_details.due_date: One hour after the tutorial session in Weeks 1–5, 7, 9, 11 and 12. Tutorial submissions in Weeks 7, 9 and 11 each cover the tutorial questions from two consecutive weeks (Weeks 6–7, 8–9 and 10–11, respectively).
assessment_details.task_description: There will be 9 Tutorial Submissions throughout the semester. Weekly tutorial questions will be provided in Weeks 1–12 to reinforce lecture concepts and develop the skills required for the practicals, commodity project and final exam. Students are encouraged to attend the tutorial sessions, where the teaching team will be available to provide assistance. Tutorial Submissions 1–5 correspond to the tutorial questions from Weeks 1–5, respectively. To avoid multiple assessment deadlines in the same week as the practical reports, Tutorial Submissions 6–8 each combine the tutorial questions from two consecutive weeks (Weeks 6–7, 8–9 and 10–11, respectively). Tutorial Submission 9 covers the tutorial questions from Week 12. Each Tutorial Submission is worth 1 mark, except Tutorial Submissions 6–8, which are each worth 2 marks. The Tutorial assessment contributes a total of 12 marks to the course. All tutorial sheets, including questions and supporting guidance, are provided at the start of the semester, allowing students to work ahead if required. Marks are awarded based on the problem-solving approach and methodology, not only the final answers. Students must clearly show their working and reasoning. Students must submit their solutions before the specified deadline for each Tutorial Submission. Late submissions will not be accepted once solutions are released. All tutorial questions within a Tutorial Submission carry equal weight. This task has been designed to evaluate your understanding of the concepts covered in this course and to assess your abilities in applying these concepts to authentic and complex problems. For these tutorial exercises, you may choose to use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) technologies to support your learning, e.g. through helping to ensure that you correctly understand the problem. However, to pass this assessment, you are required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of your written submission independent of AI and MT tools. A failure to reference your use of generative AI or MT use may therefore constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
All Tutorial Assignments must be submitted electronically via Blackboard. Late submissions will not be accepted, as solutions will be released following each tutorial.
Students must submit a single file for each Tutorial Assignment containing all required answers and supporting working.
It is the student's responsibility to ensure that the correct file is uploaded and that the submission is complete, legible, and successfully submitted before the deadline.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Tutorial Submissions are designed to provide flexibility. Weekly tutorial sheets, including questions and supporting guidance, are available from the beginning of the semester, allowing students to work ahead where appropriate.
Although Tutorial Submissions are made on nine occasions during the semester, the assessment is based on the 12 weeks of tutorial questions. Only the best 10 of the 12 weekly tutorial sets contribute to the final Tutorial mark. This allows students to miss or perform poorly on up to two weeks of tutorial questions without penalty.
To avoid multiple assessment deadlines in the same week as the practical reports, Tutorial Submissions in Weeks 7, 9 and 11 each combine the tutorial questions from two consecutive weeks.
Extensions or deferrals for Tutorial Submissions are generally not granted, as students have the opportunity to complete and submit work ahead of time.
In exceptional circumstances, such as serious unavoidable disruptions lasting more than two weeks, students should contact the teaching team as soon as possible and follow the University’s Special Consideration procedures. Where possible, students are encouraged to make use of the flexibility built into the assessment structure by completing and submitting work in advance.
Late submission
Late submissions will not be accepted under any circumstances. Since Tutorial Assignment solutions will be released following each tutorial, submissions received after the release of solutions will not be marked.
Students are strongly advised to submit their work well before the deadline to avoid issues related to technical difficulties or last-minute delays. Failure to submit on time will result in a mark of zero for that Tutorial Assignment.

assessment_details.title: Commodity Assignment - team oral presentation
assessment_details.due_date: 27/10/2026 - 28/10/2026 In class presentations (during scheduled workshop and tutorial sessions of week 13).
assessment_details.task_description: The members of your team are working on an assignment to identify the process options and technologies used for the production of a selected metal. You and your team have been asked to make an oral presentation of your findings. Oral presentation (10%) Students are to design and present their material in a professional manner, as if the audience was the board of a company. The software platform to be used is PowerPoint. Make sure you submit your presentation slide deck 24 hours prior to the scheduled presentation time. Each team member will present one part of the report. Each team will be allocated a total of 20 minutes for their oral presentation, subject to adjustment based on the number of groups. Of this time, 15 minutes are designated for the presentation itself, followed by 5 minutes for questions and answers. The session chair will provide time warnings at 5 minutes and 1 minute before the end of the presentation. Practicing before the presentation is recommended for each team to ensure their timing is correct and to improve the standard of the presentation. Presentations must not be in the form of reading the materials from a written text. This assessment task evaluates students' abilities, skills and knowledge without the aid of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT). Students are advised that the use of AI or MT technologies to develop responses is strictly prohibited and may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 11 (27 Jul - 18 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Biweekly assignment workshops The biweekly assignment workshops are designed to support students in preparing for practical sessions, writing practical reports, and working on the commodity project. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Weekly tutorials The weekly tutorials reinforce key concepts introduced in the prerecorded lectures through guided instruction and collaborative problem-solving, enabling students to effectively apply their knowledge to mineral separation and metal extraction scenarios. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 4 To Week 8 (17 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Practicals The three laboratory practicals provide students with hands-on experience in executing key mineral processing and metal extraction techniques. Conducted in groups and assessed through written reports, these sessions also develop students' teamwork and scientific communication skills. Sub-activity: Activities include: Drop Weight (8%), Leaching (8%), Solvent Extraction (9%). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L05, L06

Student Presentations The Commodity Project Presentation is a comprehensive group assessment that addresses all course aims and learning outcomes—except Learning Outcome 3 (Practical Proficiency)—with a strong emphasis on teamwork and communication. Students are required to deliver an in-depth analysis of the metallurgical processing of a selected metal, focusing on its mineralogy, processing routes, and the sustainability of production methods. Presentations will also incorporate aspects of commodity markets, economic considerations, and group collaboration. Please note that group presentations will be scheduled during tutorial time slots in Week13. Sub-activity: Assignment workshops and guest lecture. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05, L06
